result.topic_en: Riemann counts the conditions the coefficients of a linear differential equation must satisfy so that the solutions are free of branching at given points (all exponents being integers and the expansions containing no logarithms), via Maclaurin-series expansions, the indicial (determining) equation and the vanishing of leading coefficients, and relates this to the number of free constants in the coefficient functions.

items.english: The functions could only be determined so that y_1, ..., y_n belong to a given class if the number of arbitrary constants remaining in them is not smaller than the number of conditions they must satisfy.
